messages: Support check failed: the claim that “The case highlights challenges in ensuring impartial juries in high‑profile prosecutions” is not directly supported by any cited passage; the cited pages discuss voir dire arguments but do not contain this summary statement.

Attribution check failed: the claim “According to Petitioner, petitioner noted that ordinary practice would only be altered in rare cases involving a wave of public passion” attributes the remark to the Petitioner, yet the evidence attributes the remark to Mr. Srinivasan, not to the Petitioner themselves.

Attribution check failed: the claim that “The case highlights challenges in ensuring impartial juries in high‑profile prosecutions” attributes the observation to “Petitioner and Respondent,” but neither party is recorded as making that exact statement in the transcript.

Opinion distinction check failed: the same “high‑profile prosecutions” claim is presented as a factual statement, whereas it is an evaluative opinion about the case’s significance and should be labeled as such.
Overstatement check failed: the aforementioned claim overstates the record by asserting the case “highlights challenges” without explicit support, constituting an overstatement of the evidence.
